sections.h2: Recording a deed in Alcona County
sections.html:
Deeds and mortgages for Alcona County property are filed with the Register of Deeds in Harrisville. Call 989-724-9450 (fax 989-724-9459). The office is the official recording point for papers that touch real estate, and it works under a uniform state system.

It accepts warranty and quitclaim deeds, mortgages with their assignments and discharges, land contracts, liens and releases, easements, rights of way, oil and gas leases, plats, surveys, land corners and court orders. It also takes passport applications.

Counter staff cannot draft your deed or answer legal questions, so lean on a lawyer or the closing agent for that. The county closes on holidays such as Columbus Day, Thanksgiving and the Friday after, so phone ahead before you carry a signed original to the courthouse.

sections.h2: Fees at the Alcona County counter
sections.html:
Recording costs $30.00 per paper regardless of length, a figure fixed in MCL 600.2567. A few add-ons exist:

  • $3.00 extra for every further instrument when one document assigns or discharges several.
  • $1.00 a page for photocopies of the record, with $5.00 on top to certify.
  • $5.00 for the treasurer's tax certificate, which spans up to five property descriptions, then 20 cents per added description.

Mailing a deed in has quirks. Enclose a stamped, self-addressed return envelope. If your check overshoots the fee by $10.00 or less, the county keeps the difference, so total the charges before you send anything.

sections.h2: Which papers need the treasurer's certificate first?
sections.html:
Warranty deeds, land contracts and their assignments, condominium master deeds, subdivision plats and any deed that conveys with a warranty must arrive with a certificate from the Treasurer's Office, 989-724-9420.

Make this stop first on your errand list, since the certificate travels with the deed to the register. Holding a different form, such as a quitclaim? Ask the register whether the same rule reaches it.

The same counter can tell you whether any tax is still unpaid on the parcel. Knowing that number before you pick a closing date avoids a last-minute surprise.

sections.h2: Michigan transfer tax on an Alcona County sale
sections.html:
Two levies fall on the seller. The county charges $0.55 for each $500 of value (MCL 207.504) and the state charges $3.75 for each $500 (MCL 207.525). Any leftover amount is rounded up to a full $500.

County$0.55Seller

Both levels$4.30Seller

The county treasurer collects within 15 days of delivery (MCL 207.523). Put the full price on the face of the deed, or file a value affidavit with it. Ask the closing agent to total the tax on your settlement statement so you see the figure before you sign.

sections.h2: Can a family transfer avoid the transfer tax?
sections.html:
Often yes. MCL 207.526 carves out gifts inside a family, which is the usual case for heirs and aging owners.

  • Parent to child, including a stepchild or adopted child.
  • Grandparent to grandchild, including step and adopted grandchildren.
  • Spouses creating or ending a tenancy by the entireties.
  • Any instrument carrying consideration under $100.
  • A corrective deed that confirms title the grantee already holds.

If you paid and then learn an exemption applied, the state Treasury Department takes refund requests.

sections.h2: Why might Alcona County turn a deed away?
sections.html:
Michigan's recording act, MCL 565.201, gives a register grounds to refuse papers that break its layout rules. Four checks cover most trouble:

  • Leave a clear top margin of 2 1/2 inches on page one.
  • Open with a single line that names the event, such as "Warranty Deed."
  • Use 10-point or larger type in black ink on white 20-pound stock.
  • Print the drafter's name and business address on the paper.

Keep one event per sheet. A first line claiming two recordable events, such as a deed plus a release, bars recording. Ask your title agent to review the deed before signing, since a rejected paper can push back a closing.

sections.h2: Other Alcona County offices that touch a sale
sections.html:
Several county desks can matter when a house sells, and the directory on the county home page gives each one's line.

  • Treasurer, 989-724-9420: tax certificates and balances.
  • Equalization, 989-724-9430: assessed and taxable values.
  • Building Department, 989-724-9440: permits.
  • County Clerk, 989-724-9410, and Probate Court, 989-724-9490: records and estate matters when the owner has died.

Alcona County sits in Michigan's 23rd Circuit, shared with Arenac, Iosco and Oscoda counties. An heir selling an inherited house should ask Probate Court what paperwork the deed needs before anything goes to the register.

Zoning, permits and assessments sit with townships and the county, not with the register. Call Equalization or the Building Department if a permit or valuation question could hold up your sale.

Harrisville is the sole city and the county seat, and Lincoln is the village. The county has about 10,556 residents spread over 1,791 square miles, 62 percent of which is water, mostly Lake Huron and inland lakes such as Hubbard Lake. Many properties are lakefront, seasonal or inherited, and about 89.6 percent of housing is occupied by its owner.

That mix affects a sale. A seasonal or inherited house may have an old survey, a septic system and a tax history spread across several years, so gather the deed, the tax certificate and any permit records before you list. If the owner has died, start with Probate Court so the right person signs the deed, and ask the Treasurer whether any tax is outstanding before a closing date is set.

sections.h2: Selling an Alcona County house: a short checklist
sections.html:
Here is the usual order of steps for a seller who needs the deed recorded without delay:

  1. Call the Treasurer at 989-724-9420 for the tax balance and the certificate, if the deed is a warranty deed.
  2. Have a lawyer or title agent draft the deed to the layout rules above.
  3. Confirm the price on the deed, or prepare a value affidavit.
  4. Pay the $30.00 recording fee, plus any add-ons, and the transfer tax within 15 days.
  5. Keep copies. The register can furnish certified copies at $1.00 a page plus $5.00 to certify.

If the house is vacant, inherited or behind on tax, a cash as-is sale can shorten the list, since you do not have to wait on a buyer's lender. You are free to decline any offer. Whichever way you sell, confirm with the register before you mail anything, since the office can tell you the exact total to include with the paper.

faqs.q: What is the filing price for a deed in Alcona County?
faqs.a: It is $30.00 a document. A paper that assigns or discharges several instruments adds $3.00 for each extra, and copies of records cost $1.00 a page.

faqs.q: Who must pay the transfer tax in an Alcona County sale?
faqs.a: The seller must, since MCL 207.523 puts the liability on the grantor. The county treasurer expects payment inside 15 days from delivery of the deed.

faqs.q: Is a treasurer's certificate required before an Alcona County warranty deed is recorded?
faqs.a: Yes. The Treasurer's Office issues it at 989-724-9420 for $5.00 per document with up to five descriptions.

faqs.q: Can a deed go to the Alcona County register by mail?
faqs.a: Yes, if you add a stamped return envelope addressed to yourself. Any mailed overpayment of $10.00 or under becomes county revenue.

faqs.q: Is there an online search for Alcona County land records?
faqs.a: Yes, two fee-based tools: Laredo, which works by subscription, and Tapestry. Ask the register at 989-724-9450 how to sign up for Laredo.
